sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Pinellas County?
sections.html:
The Pinellas County Tax Collector sends and collects the bill, while the Pinellas County Property Appraiser sets the value and decides exemptions. The tax collector's site is pinellastaxcollector.gov and the appraiser's is pcpao.gov.

The tax collector's home page says 2026 property taxes paid in November receive a 4 percent discount, and it offers online payment and a network of kiosks. The appraiser's page lists 437,624 real property parcels and 57,476 tangible personal property accounts, so the office handles a large roll for a small county.

Pinellas has 24 municipalities, and a parcel may sit in a city or in unincorporated land. Your bill is built from the county, the school board and any city or special district that covers the parcel. Look up your parcel before you assume what the total will be.

sections.h2: What is the Pinellas County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
Florida runs one calendar for every county, and Pinellas follows it. Values are fixed as of January 1, exemption applications are due March 1, notices of proposed taxes go out in August, and bills arrive in November.

Florida property tax calendar as printed by the Department of Revenue, which Pinellas follows
WhenWhat happens
January 1Property is assessed at just value as of this date
March 1Deadline to file for exemptions and classifications with the property appraiser
April 1Deadline for tangible personal property returns on Form DR-405
AugustNotice of Proposed Property Taxes (TRIM notice) is mailed
Within 25 days of the noticePetition to the value adjustment board on a value challenge
NovemberTax bills are sent; 4% discount for payment in November
December to FebruaryDiscount of 3%, then 2%, then 1%
April 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent
By June 1Tax certificates sold on unpaid items

A denial of an exemption, classification or portability gives you 30 days from the mailing date of the denial letter to petition the value adjustment board. Petition forms are filed with the clerk of the court.

sections.h2: How do I lower the Pinellas County tax bill?
sections.html:
File the homestead exemption if you live in the house, and challenge the value if the notice looks wrong. Neither works after the deadline, so mark March 1 and the 25 days after the August notice.

  • Homestead: the first $25,000 applies to all levies including school taxes, and up to $25,000 more applies to assessed value above $50,000 for non-school levies. The owner must make the home the permanent residence by January 1 and file Form DR-501.
  • Save Our Homes: after the first year, annual growth in a homestead's assessed value is limited to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. The state chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • Non-homestead property: assessed value growth is limited to 10 percent a year.
  • Seniors and veterans: a county or city may adopt extra exemptions for owners 65 or older. Veterans with a service-connected disability may qualify for a $5,000 reduction, and totally and permanently disabled veterans for more. Ask the appraiser which ones apply to your address.

A homeowner who cannot pay a high bill has two more tools. The tax collector can set up an installment plan if you apply by May 1 of the assessment year, and a homestead owner can file Form DR-570 by March 31 to defer part of the tax.

sections.h2: What did Amendment 3 change for Pinellas County owners?
sections.html:
Florida voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026, and the changes to homestead exemptions begin with the 2027 tax year. The Escambia County tax collector states that it does not change the 2026 bill. The Pinellas appraiser's home page says its website is being updated to reflect the amendment.

For a seller, the timing matters. The 2026 bill reflects values and exemptions as of January 1, 2026, and it is due on the usual schedule with the usual November discount. Check the appraiser's pages for how new exemption amounts will apply before you advertise next year's taxes to a buyer.

sections.h2: What is Pinellas County like for a property owner?
sections.html:
Pinellas is Florida's most densely populated county, with 3,425 people per square mile on 280 square miles, according to the county's fast facts page. It stretches 38 miles long and 15 miles at its broadest point, with 588 miles of coastline and 35 miles of beaches. The 2020 Census counted 959,107 people.

Clearwater is the county seat and St. Petersburg is the largest city. The county reports about 4,500 miles of paved roads and more than 400 bridges. The Gandy Causeway in 1924 was the first span across Tampa Bay, and the Sunshine Skyway opened in 1954 to connect Pinellas with Manatee County.

The appraiser's roll shows what kind of housing dominates: 241,442 single family units, 103,445 condo units, 22,112 townhome or PUD units, 44,323 manufactured home units and 101,180 multifamily rental units. A condo owner and a single family owner can face very different bills, so read the parcel record for your own unit type.

The appraiser's main courthouse office is at 315 Court Street, 2nd Floor, Clearwater, with hours of 8AM to 5PM Monday to Friday and a phone line at (727) 464-3207. It also lists North County, Mid County and South County offices. The Mid County office is co-located with the Tax Collector at 13025 Starkey Rd in Largo.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Pinellas County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax is paid out of closing proceeds, so a seller who is behind should ask the tax collector for a payoff figure early. Taxes become delinquent on April 1, and a tax certificate can then be sold on the unpaid amount.

Certificate buyers bid down the interest rate in quarter percent steps. The holder may not demand payment from the owner until two years after April 1 of the year of issuance, and may apply for a tax deed after that period, with an application fee of $75. At the sale, the clerk runs the auction and interest on the bid accrues at 1.5 percent per month.

  • Homestead property with less than $250 delinquent goes to the county rather than to auction.
  • The opening bid on a homestead includes one half of the latest assessed value.
  • Persons noticed before a tax deed sale include the titleholder, mortgagees and contract for deed buyers.

Selling before a tax deed application is the cleanest way out, because the buyer's title company pays the certificate off at closing. A sale also resets the assessment, which is why a seller's old bill does not predict the buyer's.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Pinellas County?
faqs.a: The Pinellas County Tax Collector. The property appraiser sets values and exemptions, but the tax collector sends the bill and takes payment.

faqs.q: What discount do I get for paying Pinellas County property tax early?
faqs.a: It is 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. The tax collector's page highlights the 4 percent November discount for 2026 taxes.

faqs.q: When do Pinellas County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1 following the November billing. Tax certificates on unpaid items are sold by June 1.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Pinellas County property value?
faqs.a: File a petition with the clerk of the court within 25 days of the August Notice of Proposed Property Taxes. For a denied exemption, petition the value adjustment board within 30 days of the denial letter's mailing.

faqs.q: Does Amendment 3 change my 2026 Pinellas County bill?
faqs.a: No. A Florida tax collector's notice says it does not change the 2026 bill, and the homestead changes start with the 2027 tax year. Confirm details for your parcel with the Pinellas property appraiser.
